Cp.bar_b_note: A and B are the same frame: the HUD is now limited to the corners, as in Palworld, but the panels are muddy brown-black rather than translucent blue-grey, the hotbar block is heavy, the whole frame is dimmed, and the bed blanket is dark red/oxblood on a friendly interior element.

Ut.bar_b_note: The Stormcapra model (white fleece, dark curled horns, blue accents) is at the owner style bar and carries it; A's rearing hit react and lying faint read clearly, but B's hit react barely differs from standing and its faint mid/end tip the body sideways and hover it off the floor.

Oc.bar_b_note: The nodes are tiny generic shapes (a pale cluster for orb_basic, a red-brown box for travel_pack, a small glowing plant for attack_tonic) on a uniform saturated grass carpet, with no haze or light shafts to give Valheim-class depth.

Vh.bar_b_note: B's aftermaths are site-specific (a fallen banner, an opened cage with a freed villager, a smoking doused brazier), but both sides sit on smeared low-resolution terrain and flat tiling tunnel walls, and in A enemy banners stay standing after the win in rows 1, 3 and 5.

Nh.bar_b_note: A's timber frame (diagonal brace, top cap, stone footing) reads as built, but it is still a lone thin panel; B is a blown-out white card with no cap or footing; on both sides the flat-shaded pale boulder and the painted-card mountains sink the finish.

Ty.bar_b_note: The pickups now have distinct forms (wrapped candy, a cloth bundle, a pink flask), but they are a few pixels tall on an even grass carpet, and the blobby low-detail tree canopies read short of Palworld's finish.

Ky.bar_b_note: In the strike and absorbing frames the camera looks down over a huge blurred, cropped companion body that fills the bottom third, so the player-to-target link is lost; the orb glow is the only thing that reads.

Mq.bar_b_note: The grey-haired, bearded elder has clean shading, readable eyes and a green/brown palette that fits the meadows; his rounder cartoon proportions sit slightly off the naturalistic creature style.

Qb.bar_b_note: The hurt frames now tilt or rear, but the creatures are small mid-ground subjects with no rim light against busy dark foliage, and a large dark foreground bush fills the lower right of every frame.

Tp.bar_b_note: Brooktail, Pipwing and Bramblebun all stand at or below the trainer's shoulder, which breaks the 'every creature taller than 1.80 m' rule and leaves them as specks against the scene.

Yq.bar_b_note: Bramblebun, Pipwing and the fainted Mossthief all lose their lower outlines in grass of the same value, so ground contact cannot be read; the meadow backdrop is pleasant but flat-lit.

Ne.bar_b_note: Mira, Tam and Oskar are now distinct world characters who match their portraits in a cozy, cohesive village, but the flat midday light and the absence of atmosphere or a time-of-day grade keep it short of Valheim-class light.

top_changes.change: Scale every normal creature above the 1.80 m trainer and push it to the owner style bar (rim light, value separation from the grass); this lifts Tp, Yq, Qb, Ky and Oc together.
Break the uniform grass carpet into groves, edges and clearings, thin the grass around creature and pickup footprints, and add distance haze, shafts and a warm time-of-day grade.
Reframe the catch camera as an over-shoulder shot that keeps companion, player and target in frame, and restyle the HUD panels to translucent blue-grey with a lighter hotbar.
